title: Research
text: My research is in geometric topology, with an emphasis on essential surfaces, essential and measured laminations, and taut foliations in 3-manifolds. I am particularly interested in using normal surface theory and branched surfaces to describe spaces of geometric objects and to make their structure accessible to computation.

title: Research
text:
Publications and Preprints

Growth Rate of Essential Surfaces via Measured Laminations
Brevan Ellefsen, 2026. arXiv:2608.08833

I relate the dimensions of Hatcher’s measured lamination spaces to normal surface theory. Under the hypotheses of the paper, the polynomial growth exponent for closed orientable essential surfaces, counted up to isotopy by a bound on negative Euler characteristic, is the dimension of the space of closed measured laminations. This gives an intrinsic geometric interpretation of the surface-counting exponent, analogous to the role of measured laminations in counting curves on surfaces.

title: Research
text:
Current Research

Essential Faces and Surface Counts

I am extending the surface-counting results to compact surfaces with boundary and to 3-manifolds under weaker hypotheses. A central part of this work is to understand which faces of the normal solution space carry essential surfaces, and how their dimensions and isotopy relations determine growth exponents. This is part of a follow-up project to the closed-surface counting paper.



Least-Weight Laminations

I am developing a normal-surface theory of least-weight representatives of essential measured laminations. The goal is to construct normal representatives that minimize combinatorial weight in their isotopy classes, and to organize them using faces of the normal solution space and incompressible branched surfaces. Understanding the identifications arising from isotopy would then give a concrete normal-coordinate model of Hatcher’s measured lamination space.



Volume Bounds on Growth

I am investigating how the dimensions of measured lamination spaces vary with the geometry of the underlying hyperbolic 3-manifold. In particular, I am interested in bounds in terms of hyperbolic volume and, through the connection with surface counts, in how volume constrains the growth of essential surfaces.



Minimal Laminations

I am studying when an essential lamination admits a representative whose leaves are all minimal for a suitable ambient metric. This project is motivated by least-area incompressible surfaces and by the relationship between taut foliations and minimal leaves. I am particularly interested in approaches that construct the metric explicitly, including methods inspired by dynamics and transverse measures.

title: Research
text:
Other Interests
My broader interests include pseudo-Anosov flows, veering triangulations, hyperbolic geometry, knot theory, normal and almost-normal surfaces, and connections between 3-manifolds and Teichmüller theory. I am particularly interested in methods that can be made computational.
I am also interested in dynamical problems, particularly those that can be tackled using ergodic and specification techniques.

title: Brevan Ellefsen
text:
I am a PhD candidate in mathematics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, advised by Nathan Dunfield. I expect to complete my PhD in May 2027. I work in geometric topology, particularly essential surfaces, essential and measured laminations, and taut foliations in 3-manifolds.
My research focuses on the interplay between laminations and surfaces. I use normal surface theory and branched surfaces to study spaces of measured laminations and the growth of essential surface counts. I am also interested in pseudo-Anosov flows and in constructing ambient metrics for which the leaves of an essential lamination are minimal.


My preprint Growth Rate of Essential Surfaces via Measured Laminations is available on the arXiv. It relates measured lamination space to normal surface theory and gives an intrinsic geometric interpretation of the growth exponent for closed essential surface counts under the hypotheses of the paper.
My current projects include extending these counts to compact surfaces with boundary and developing a normal-coordinate model of measured lamination space using least-weight laminations. I am also investigating the relationship between hyperbolic volume and surface growth, and the existence of minimal representatives of essential laminations.
See my research page for more about my work.
In spring 2026, I was a Program Associate at SLMath for Topological and Geometric Structures in Low Dimensions. I also organize the UIUC Geometric Topology Seminar and mentor undergraduates through the Directed Reading Program. My CV includes my education, talks, teaching, and service.
